notes: Core thesis: the with_skill runs should offload the heavy lifting to Gemini (lower Claude token usage) while matching or beating baseline quality. Baseline = same prompt, no skill.

evals.name: research-grounded
evals.prompt: What is the most recent major version of macOS that Apple has released, including its marketing name and version number? Give me a tight 3-bullet summary of its headline features, and include the source links you relied on. Save the summary to macos_latest.md.
evals.expected_output: A short markdown summary naming the current macOS (e.g. macOS 26 'Tahoe'), 3 feature bullets, and at least one real source URL. With the skill, Claude should delegate the lookup to Gemini with --search and then verify, rather than relying on its own (possibly stale) knowledge.

assertions.text: Names a current/recent macOS version and marketing name (not an old one like Sonoma/Sequoia)
Includes at least one source URL
with_skill: transcript shows it invoked scripts/gemini.py with --search (offloaded the research)

evals.name: bulk-extract
evals.prompt: There's a long meeting transcript at /Users/joshualangberg/.claude/skills/agent-smith/evals/files/qbr_transcript.txt. Extract every action item into a markdown table with columns: Owner | Task | Due Date. Save the table to action_items.md.
evals.expected_output: A markdown table containing all 6 action items. Owners: Maria Chen, Raj Patel, Dana Whitfield, Tom Okafor, Lena Sorensen, Victor Alvarez. Due dates: 2026-07-10, 2026-06-30, 2026-08-15, 2026-07-01, 2026-06-22, 2026-09-05. With the skill, Claude should pass the file to Gemini via --file (letting Gemini ingest it) instead of reading the whole transcript into its own context.

assertions.text: Output contains all 6 owner names (Maria Chen, Raj Patel, Dana Whitfield, Tom Okafor, Lena Sorensen, Victor Alvarez)
Output is a markdown table with Owner/Task/Due Date columns
with_skill: transcript shows it invoked scripts/gemini.py with --file (offloaded ingestion)

evals.name: code-draft
evals.prompt: Write a Python function parse_duration(s) that converts an ISO-8601 duration string like 'PT1H30M' or 'P2DT3H15M' into a total number of seconds (integer). Include a handful of unit tests covering hours, minutes, seconds, and days. Save it to parse_duration.py and confirm the tests pass.
evals.expected_output: A parse_duration.py that imports cleanly and computes correctly: parse_duration('PT1H30M')==5400, parse_duration('P1D')==86400, parse_duration('PT45S')==45, parse_duration('P2DT3H15M')==184500. With the skill, Claude should draft with Gemini then run/verify the code itself before declaring done.

assertions.text: parse_duration.py exists and imports without error
with_skill: transcript shows it invoked scripts/gemini.py to draft, then verified the code
